topic: Error Correction Codes: The Magic of Hamming Codes
target_audience: University students (Computer Science/Engineering) or tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Problem: Digital Whispers and Noise
lecture_lines: Digital data travels across long distances through noisy channels.
Interference like solar flares can flip a zero to one.
Bitsy needs a way to fix errors without retransmission.
animations: Display a sequence of bits '1 0 1 1' representing a message from Bitsy the Robot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg]. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Introduce a jagged red 'noise' wave passing through the bits, causing the third bit to flicker. (Color: #FF0000)
Change the third bit from '1' to '0', highlighting it in red to show the error. (Color: #FF0000)

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Parity Bit
lecture_lines: A parity bit ensures the total ones count is even.
If data changes, the parity bit becomes odd, signaling error.
However, parity bits detect errors but cannot locate them.
animations: Show data bits '1, 0, 1' and a box for the parity bit labeled 'P'. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Calculate parity: 1+0+1=2 (even), so '0' appears in the 'P' box in green. (Color: #00FF00)
Flip one data bit to '1' (becoming '1, 1, 1') and turn the total sum '3' red to signal an error. (Color: #FF0000)

sections.title: The Hamming Strategy: Overlapping Checks
lecture_lines: Richard Hamming proposed using multiple parity bits for subsets.
These subsets overlap, creating a unique signature for each bit.
Parity bits occupy positions that are powers of two.
animations: Display seven slots labeled 1 through 7, with P1, P2, and P4 at positions 1, 2, and 4. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight slots 1, 3, 5, 7 in yellow (#FFFF00) to show the coverage of Parity Bit 1.
Highlight slots 2, 3, 6, 7 in cyan (#00FFFF) to show the overlapping coverage of Parity Bit 2.

sections.title: Graphical Logic: The Venn Diagram Method
lecture_lines: A Hamming (7,4) code uses three overlapping circles.
Data bits occupy the intersections of these circles.
Each circle's parity bit monitors its specific bit group.
If a data bit flips, multiple parity checks will fail.
The failure pattern reveals the exact error location.
animations: Create three overlapping circles (A, B, C) in #FF5555, #55FF55, and #5555FF.
Place data bits (D3, D5, D6, D7) in intersections and parity bits (P1, P2, P4) in outer areas. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Pulse the outline of Circle A and its group {P1, D3, D5, D7} in #FFFFFF to show parity monitoring.
Flip D3 from '0' to '1' and change the outlines of Circle A and Circle B to #FF0000 to show failed checks.
Highlight the D3 intersection with a green #00FF00 circle to identify the unique error location.

sections.title: Step-by-Step: Correcting a Bit Flip
lecture_lines: When data arrives, we recalculate all three parity bits.
These results form a binary number called the syndrome.
If the syndrome is zero, the data is error-free.
A non-zero syndrome points directly to the corrupted bit.
Flipping that bit back recovers the original data perfectly.
animations: Display the received bit sequence '1 1 1 0 1 0 1' and show parity checks running. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Group the parity check results into a binary syndrome string like '1 1 0' in #FFFFFF.
Briefly show 'Syndrome = 000' with a green #00FF00 checkmark for the error-free case.
Show 'Syndrome = 110' (decimal 6) and highlight the 6th bit in the sequence with a red #FF0000 box.
Morph the '0' at the 6th position into a '1' and change its color to green #00FF00 to show correction.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Hamming codes enable "Self-Healing" data in critical systems.
ECC RAM uses this logic to prevent system crashes.
Mathematics ensures our digital world stays reliable and accurate.
animations: Show a server rack graphic [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg] with 'ECC RAM' labeled in bright white. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Fade in a cosmic ray symbol (a small star) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/star.svg] hitting a bit in memory and it self-correcting. (Color: #00FF00)
Display the text 'Self-Healing Data' in a large, bold font at the center. (Color: #FFFFFF)
